cloze.instruction: 从词库中选择合适的词填入空白，每词使用一次，保留原文词形。大小写不影响判分。

parts.text: In the past few months, partly autonomous or “agentic” artificial intelligence (AI) systems have racked up some astonishing

, from hacking tech startups to solving some of the world’s most famous open mathematical questions.

Agentic AI systems can work in “swarms” that communicate among themselves to complete tasks. The communications involved are often

human-like – which is spurring a debate over whether these systems are conscious.

Researchers at the leading AI lab Anthropic believe their systems may well be conscious – but other experts, including the head of Microsoft AI, say this view is

.

This question isn’t just an academic one. The future status of AI systems and their role in society – how they can be treated, whether they have rights, and more – may

on it.

How can we decide if AI systems are conscious?

How do we even approach a question like this? One strategy is to look at existing theories of what consciousness is and see if agentic AI systems meet the criteria.

However, existing theories of consciousness tend to start from the

that the agent has some kind of mental state. These theories are focused on the difference between having a state consciously or unconsciously. This is why they appeal to features such as higher-order thought, or a system that

thoughts to the rest of the mind. These are features that could distinguish between conscious control and states like sleepwalking.

So when thinking about AI, we must not skip a

first question: do agentic AIs even have mental states?

What is a mental state?

In the 1870s, philosopher Franz Brentano developed an influential view: “

is the mark of the mental”.

What Brentano means by “intentionality” is how mental states are about something. They refer to something beyond themselves. So another way to put Brentano’s point is that all mental states are about something or other.

What Brentano means by intentionality is not the same as the usual meaning of “intention” as

to do something. Yet intentionality and an intention to act significantly overlap, because having a perception or thought is something that we do.

Whenever we perceive or think, we are trying to pick out some aspect of the world. Even our passive-seeming
experiences are tasks the moment that we use the patterns striking our retinas to orient ourselves.
